sentences.text: Westralichthys represents an extinct genus comprising a single species of dunkleosteoid fish.
This creature is a member of the class Placodermi, known for their bony armor.
Scientists estimate the animal reached a length of 3 meters.
There is only one recorded fossil occurrence of this genus in the Paleobiology Database.
The genus is known from a single fossil skull identified as WAM 86.9.664.
The name Westralichthys combines 'Western' for the Australian state and 'ichthys' for fish.
The genus was first described by Long in 1987.
Westralichthys belongs to the superfamily Dunkleosteoidea and is related to the giant Dunkleosteus.
The animal is classified within the family Dinichthyidae.
Fossils were found in the Virgin Hills Formation of Western Australia dating to the Middle Famennian stage of the Late Devonian.
The species lived between 372.15 and 358.86 million years ago during the Famennian.
